English around the world

From a handful of dialects in 5th-century Britain to more than 1.35 billion speakers today: when English reached each country, and how many people speak it now.

Scroll to move through time. Tap any country for its facts.

Sources

  • Speakers by country: List of countries by English-speaking population, Wikipedia (national censuses and surveys, 2003–2025; accessed November 2026).
  • 5–7 million first-language speakers around 1600 and about 250 million by the 1950s: David Crystal, cited in Dick Leith, “English — colonial to postcolonial” (Routledge, 2020).
  • Over 1.35 billion speakers: “Influence of the development of the English language”, International Journal of Literature and Languages (2024).
  • Aviation English: ICAO Annex 10 recommendation (1951), via Aviation English, Wikipedia; Level 4 requirement applicable from 5 March 2008 and retesting: ICAO Annex 1 language proficiency provisions.
  • Arrival years mark the first lasting English-speaking settlement, trading post or rule, using standard historical dates. Countries without one are shown from 1945, when English spread worldwide as a second language.
  • Map: Natural Earth (public domain), via world-atlas. Small island nations are not on this map. 3D: three.js (MIT).
